name: Learn essential phrases for one specific trip
blurb: Not the language — thirty phrases and the pronunciation to be understood. It measurably changes how you are treated as a visitor.
gear: A phrasebook or an app with audio
steps: Learn the courtesies first: hello, please, thank you, excuse me, sorry, goodbye. These do most of the social work.
Learn the transactional set: numbers to twenty, how much, where is, I would like, the bill please.
Learn the critical set: I do not understand, do you speak English, I am allergic to…, help, and where is the hospital.
Focus on pronunciation over vocabulary. Thirty words said understandably beat three hundred said unintelligibly.
Drill with audio and a spaced-repetition deck for ten minutes a day.
Use them from the first day of the trip, badly and cheerfully.
tips: Learning to say "I do not speak much [language]" in that language is the single most useful phrase there is.
Write your allergy or dietary requirement on a card in the local language. It is far more reliable than speaking it.
proof: You complete everyday transactions on the trip in the local language without switching to English.
